purify.min.js
=============

Source:  DOMPurify 3.4.16 (https://www.npmjs.com/package/dompurify), by Cure53 and
         contributors. Dual licensed Apache-2.0 OR MPL-2.0 (both licence texts are in
         this folder: LICENSE and LICENSE-MPL).
Fetched: 2026-10-02, unmodified, from the npm tarball:
             npm pack dompurify@3.4.16
             tar -xzf dompurify-3.4.16.tgz
             cp package/dist/purify.min.js  assets/vendor/dompurify/purify.min.js
         npm integrity: sha512-sqo+pNp3qRhCIpbgRi1y8Tgk27Bo2Ry7w0dC1NBeNTdZChWjz9Xb/KOoZbRP/R6pQZ80Qw8YhXw13hWWBbMRnQ==
         purify.min.js sha256: 2c90a9b46d6463f26038a29b686e82bc91de01fdac9d5229e7cfe3b360134ea2

Why it is here: assets/js/sop.js renders author-written markdown with `marked` and
assigned the result straight to innerHTML. `marked` does not sanitise, so
<img onerror=...>, <script> and [x](javascript:...) reached the page; a user holding
action.manage_sop (a broad grant) could run script in an administrator's browser.
renderMarkdown() now passes everything through DOMPurify and, if DOMPurify is not
loaded, falls back to escaped plain text (fail closed) rather than unsanitised HTML.

Vendored, not loaded from a CDN, for the same two reasons as marked: groups run fully
disconnected, and an unpinned CDN file changes our code without a commit here.

To upgrade: `npm pack dompurify@<version>`, replace purify.min.js, update the version
and hashes above and the SBOM entry in tools/generate-sbom.php, then run
tests/test_gh_sop_xss.php.
